name: Venice
tagline: A city of water, palaces and impossible beauty.
bestMonths: Apr, May, Jun, Oct and Nov
whenBlurb: Come late spring or September for luminous light and the season in full swing; sidestep the August crush and the autumn acqua alta floods.

ourTake.lede: Stay two nights minimum so you can have the city at dawn and after the day-trippers leave on the last trains, that empty, echoing Venice is the only one worth the trouble. Cross the lagoon to Torcello or Burano for a long lunch rather than grinding through San Marco at midday. And take a water taxi from the airport at least once; arriving by boat is the whole point.
ourTake.comeIf: You want to drift through canals and Renaissance galleries with nowhere urgent to be, ideally two people and a quiet palazzo.
ourTake.skipIf: You need beaches, nightlife, or children with energy to burn, the crowds and prices will wear you down.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Aman Venice
items.description: Aman's Venetian house, a 16th-century Grand Canal palazzo with Tiepolo ceilings and just 24 rooms, private to the point of silence.

items.name: Cipriani, A Belmond Hotel, Venice
items.description: The first hotel Belmond ever owned, an island retreat with an Olympic saltwater pool and its own launch to St Mark's.

items.name: The Gritti Palace, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near Santa Maria del Giglio)
items.description: A 1475 doge's palace on the Grand Canal, Murano chandeliers, Rubelli silks and the most storied terrace in Venice.

items.name: Danieli, Venezia, A Four Seasons Hotel
items.area: Castello (Riva degli Schiavoni, near St Mark's)
items.description: Three interlinked palaces on the waterfront by the Doge's Palace, Venice's most famous grande dame, reborn under Four Seasons.

items.name: Hotel Bauer / Rosewood Venice
items.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, Campo San Moisè)
items.description: The historic Bauer on the Grand Canal, reborn under Rosewood, a landmark palazzo restoration steps from the square.

items.name: Hotel Cipriani, Palazzo Vendramin & Palazzetto
credentials: MICHELIN Three Keys (2025, as part of Belmond Hotel Cipriani)
items.description: The Cipriani's private annexe of grand suites, with a butler and lagoon-facing salon looking straight at San Marco.

items.name: The St. Regis Venice
items.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near San Moisè)
items.description: A run of restored palazzi on the Grand Canal, contemporary within, butler service and a waterfront terrace facing Santa Maria della Salute.

items.name: Hotel Metropole
items.description: A waterfront landmark packed with a collector's rooms of art and antiques, intensely, idiosyncratically Venetian.

items.name: Nolinski Venezia, Evok Collection
items.description: Paris meets Venice in the former stock-exchange building off the square, the city's most fashionable recent opening.

items.name: Ca' Sagredo Hotel
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A 15th-century palazzo and national monument on the Grand Canal, hung with frescoes by Tiepolo and Longhi, a stay inside a museum.

items.name: Violino d'Oro
items.area: San Marco (near San Moisè / Grand Canal)
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: An intimate, beautifully-crafted boutique house on a small canal square, a short walk from Piazza San Marco.

items.name: Ca' di Dio
items.area: Castello (Riva Ca' di Dio, near the Arsenale)
items.description: A 13th-century pilgrims' hospice reimagined by Patricia Urquiola, two courtyards and a calm well away from the crowds.

items.name: Londra Palace Venezia
items.description: A lagoon-front palazzo where Tchaikovsky wrote his Fourth Symphony, 53 windows onto the water, freshly and elegantly redone.

items.name: The Venice Venice Hotel
items.area: Cannaregio (Grand Canal, near Ca' d'Oro / Rialto)
items.description: A 13th-century palazzo turned 'post-Venetian' design hotel on the Grand Canal, art, vintage and a canal-level lounge.

items.name: Palazzo Venart Luxury Hotel
items.area: Santa Croce (Grand Canal, near San Stae)
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A frescoed Grand Canal palazzo with a private garden, home to the city's most decorated kitchen.

items.name: Hotel Excelsior Venice Lido Resort
items.description: A Moorish-fantasy beach palace on the Lido, the grand address of the Venice Film Festival, with a private stretch of Adriatic sand.

items.name: JW Marriott Venice Resort & Spa
items.description: A whole private lagoon island with a rooftop pool, olive groves and a spa, resort calm, ten minutes by launch from the square.

items.name: Baglioni Hotel Luna
items.area: San Marco (near Piazza San Marco / St Mark's Basin)
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Reputedly the oldest hostelry in Venice, moments from the square, with a Tiepolo-school frescoed ballroom.

items.name: Hotel Danieli Excelsior wing / Hotel Monaco & Grand Canal
items.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near San Marco Vallaresso)
items.description: A Grand Canal house at the mouth of the basin, the Ridotto's old gaming rooms within, and a terrace on the water.

items.name: Palazzina Grassi
items.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near Campo San Samuele)
items.description: Philippe Starck's playful design palazzo on the Grand Canal, the city's most fashionable small hotel.

items.name: Hotel Flora
items.area: San Marco (near Calle Larga XXII Marzo)
items.description: A family-run garden hideaway off the smart shopping street, a pocket of green calm in the middle of San Marco.

items.name: NH Collection Venezia Palazzo Barocci
items.description: A restored Gothic palazzo on the Grand Canal with canal-view rooms, grand address, gentler price.

items.name: Hotel Ai Reali
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A quietly luxurious small hotel just off the Rialto, with a rare indoor pool and spa for Venice.

items.name: Splendid Venice, Starhotels Collezione
items.description: A comfortable, characterful house in the heart of San Marco, with a roof terrace over the tiled skyline.

items.name: St Mark's Basilica (Basilica di San Marco)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: Venice's golden cathedral, over 8,000 sq m of Byzantine mosaics glinting above the nave, the jewelled Pala d'Oro altarpiece and the four bronze horses. Book a timed skip-the-line slot and add the Loggia terrace for the horses and a view over the square; shoulders and knees must be covered, and a private guide keeps a multi-generational group moving past the crowds.

items.name: Doge's Palace (Palazzo Ducale)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The pink-and-white Gothic seat of the Venetian Republic, vast council chambers hung with Tintoretto and Veronese, the golden Scala d'Oro staircase, then across the enclosed Bridge of Sighs to the old prisons. The Secret Itineraries tour (book ahead) takes you through the doge's private routes and Casanova's cell.

items.name: Piazza San Marco
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: Napoleon's 'drawing room of Europe', the only true piazza in Venice, framed by the arcaded Procuratie and the basilica. Come at first light for the empty square to yourselves, or take coffee at Caffè Florian (since 1720) with the orchestra playing; the pigeon-fed grandchildren will remember it for life.

items.name: St Mark's Campanile
items.description: The 98.6m bell tower of the basilica, rebuilt after its 1902 collapse, with a lift straight to the top. The finest panorama in the city, the whole lagoon, the red rooftops and San Giorgio across the water; go near sunset and book the timed ticket to skip the queue.

items.name: Torre dell'Orologio (St Mark's Clock Tower)
items.description: The Renaissance astronomical clock tower of 1499 above the entrance to the Mercerie, showing moon phases and the zodiac, topped by the two bronze 'Moors' who strike the hour. Visit only by pre-booked guided tour, which climbs inside past the working mechanism to the terrace beside the bell.

items.name: Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: Longhena's great white baroque dome at the mouth of the Grand Canal, built in thanks for the end of the 1630 plague. Step inside the octagon for Titian's ceiling canvases and 'Pentecost'; it is a two-minute walk from the Punta della Dogana, so pair the two on one Dorsoduro morning.

items.name: Basilica dei Frari (Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The towering brick Franciscan church that holds Titian's radiant 'Assumption of the Virgin' over the high altar, and Titian's own tomb, and Canova's pyramid monument. Quiet, cool and profoundly moving; combine with the Scuola Grande di San Rocco a minute away.

items.name: San Giorgio Maggiore
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: Palladio's serene white Benedictine church on its own island facing the piazzetta, with two Tintorettos in the chancel. Take the lift up the campanile for the classic postcard view back across the water to San Marco, far shorter queues than St Mark's own tower.

items.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The definitive collection of Venetian painting from the 14th to 18th centuries, Bellini, Giorgione, Carpaccio, Titian, Tintoretto, Veronese, and Leonardo's 'Vitruvian Man' (shown only occasionally). The anchor of the Dorsoduro 'Museum Mile'; a private guide makes two hours plenty for a family.

items.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
items.description: Peggy Guggenheim's unfinished palazzo on the Grand Canal, packed with Picasso, Pollock, Ernst, Miró, Kandinsky and Calder, plus a sculpture garden by the water. Human-scaled and light-filled, the easiest modern-art hit in Venice, with a cafe terrace for a break.

items.name: Ca' Rezzonico (Museum of 18th-Century Venice)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: A Longhena palazzo opening straight onto the Grand Canal, restored as a museum of Settecento Venice, Tiepolo ceilings, Longhi's scenes of daily life, Murano chandeliers and a reconstructed apothecary. Grand and uncrowded; the ballroom alone justifies the visit.

items.name: Punta della Dogana
items.description: The triangular former customs house at the tip of Dorsoduro, converted by Tadao Ando into a raw, luminous space for the Pinault Collection's contemporary art, Hirst, Sherman and other living names. Book jointly with its sister venue Palazzo Grassi.

items.name: Palazzo Grassi
items.description: The grandest 18th-century palace on the Grand Canal, also remodelled by Tadao Ando, staging large single-artist and thematic shows from the Pinault Collection. A calm, monumental counterpoint to the old-master churches nearby.

items.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
items.description: A confraternity hall entirely covered by more than 50 Tintoretto canvases, his life's masterwork, from the vast 'Crucifixion' to the ceiling cycle. Grab one of the mirrors provided so you can study the ceilings without craning; a minute from the Frari.

items.name: Grand Canal by vaporetto Line 1
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The world's most beautiful high street, a slow ride the full length of the Grand Canal past a parade of Gothic and Renaissance palazzi, under the Rialto and Accademia bridges. Sit at the open stern of the Line 1 boat; or, discreetly, hire a private water taxi to run it at your own pace.

items.name: Gondola ride through the back canals
items.description: The essential Venetian half-hour, glide off the Grand Canal into the silent narrow rii, under low bridges, past water-doors. Start away from the San Marco rank to avoid the jam; a private evening ride with your own boatman is the calm, romantic version for a couple or a family of four.

items.name: Traghetto crossing of the Grand Canal
items.description: The locals' shortcut, a two-euro, two-minute crossing of the Grand Canal standing up in a shared gondola, at points like Santa Sofia near the Rialto. The cheapest, most authentic gondola moment there is, and a small thrill for children learning to balance like a Venetian.

items.name: Rialto Bridge (Ponte di Rialto)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The oldest and grandest of the canal's four bridges, a single marble arch of 1591 lined with shops, framing the classic Grand Canal view of boats and palazzi. Cross at dawn for the empty stone; by day it is the busy hinge between San Marco and the market side.

items.name: Rialto Market (Mercato di Rialto)
items.description: Venice's larder for a thousand years, the Erberia fruit-and-vegetable stalls and the arcaded Pescheria fish market, busiest and best before 9am (closed Sundays, fish also Mondays). A feast of colour for the eye even without buying; the surrounding lanes hide bacari for a cicchetti graze.

items.name: T Fondaco dei Tedeschi rooftop terrace
items.description: The rooftop of the restored German merchants' house, now a luxury store beside the Rialto, opens a free 360° terrace over the bend of the Grand Canal. Slots are timed and must be booked ahead online, do it, it is the best free view in Venice.

items.name: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
items.description: A hidden multi-arched spiral staircase (bovolo means 'snail shell') tucked in a courtyard near Campo Manin, climbing to a loggia with a rooftop view over the tiled sea of the city. A short, quiet, magical detour that most day-trippers never find.

items.name: Libreria Acqua Alta
items.description: The gloriously chaotic bookshop that stacks its stock in gondolas and bathtubs against the high water, with resident cats and a 'staircase' of old books out the back leading to a canal view. Photogenic and one-of-a-kind, children love the cats and the flooded absurdity of it.

items.name: Jewish Ghetto (Ghetto Ebraico)
items.description: The world's first ghetto, established in 1516, tall, crowded houses around a quiet campo, five historic synagogues and the Jewish Museum, with kosher bakeries and restaurants nearby. Take the museum's synagogue tour to understand a moving chapter of the city's history.

items.name: Cannaregio sestiere and the Fondamenta della Misericordia
items.description: The city's most lived-in quarter, long sunny canalside fondamente lined with bacari, washing strung overhead, real Venetians going about their day. Come for an early-evening cicchetti-and-ombra crawl where the locals eat, a world away from the San Marco crush.

items.name: Madonna dell'Orto
items.description: Tintoretto's parish church in quiet northern Cannaregio, holding several of his greatest canvases and his tomb. Serene, uncrowded and richly rewarding, the sort of place a private guide brings you to feel the real Venice between the headline sights.

items.name: Ca' d'Oro (Galleria Giorgio Franchetti)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The 'golden house', the most beautiful Gothic palace on the Grand Canal, now a gallery whose treasures include Mantegna's 'St Sebastian'. Step onto its canal-side loggia for a rare inside-a-palazzo view straight down the water.

items.name: Dorsoduro and the Zattere waterfront
items.description: Venice's arty, student quarter, the buzzing Campo Santa Margherita by night, and the long, sunlit Zattere promenade along the Giudecca Canal with wide water views. A gelato on the Zattere at sunset is one of the city's simplest pleasures for all ages.

items.name: Squero di San Trovaso
items.description: One of the last working gondola boatyards, its Alpine-style wooden sheds set against a quiet canal in Dorsoduro. You watch the craftsmen from across the water as they build and repair the black boats by hand, a living workshop, best viewed from the Fondamenta opposite.

items.name: Castello and the Via Garibaldi
items.description: The broad, tree-lined Via Garibaldi in eastern Castello is where Venetians shop, gossip and eat, the least touristy stroll in the city, leading to the leafy public gardens. A genuine neighbourhood walk that grandparents and grandchildren can amble at their own pace.

items.name: Scuola Dalmata di San Giorgio degli Schiavoni
items.description: A tiny confraternity hall in Castello whose ground-floor room is wrapped in Vittore Carpaccio's jewel-like narrative cycle of St George and the dragon and St Jerome. One of the most intimate and perfect small treasures in all Venice.

items.name: Chiesa di San Zaccaria
items.description: Just behind the waterfront, this church holds Giovanni Bellini's luminous altarpiece 'San Zaccaria Altarpiece', and, for a small fee, a flooded crypt you can descend into among the old doges' tombs. An easy, atmospheric stop steps from San Marco.

items.name: Teatro La Fenice
items.description: 'The Phoenix', the opera house that has burned and risen more than once, restored in gilt and blue after the 1996 fire. Take the daytime audio-guided tour of the auditorium and royal box, or, better, book a night at the opera and dress for it.

items.name: Riva degli Schiavoni promenade
items.description: The grand waterfront esplanade sweeping east from the Doge's Palace, crossing pretty bridges past the great old hotels, with the lagoon and San Giorgio filling the view. The best evening passeggiata in the city, wide, open and unhurried.

items.name: Bridge of Sighs (Ponte dei Sospiri) viewpoint
items.description: The enclosed white baroque bridge of 1603 that carried prisoners from the Doge's Palace to the new prisons, the last glimpse of the lagoon they 'sighed' over. See it from the Ponte della Paglia on the waterfront; you cross it from inside on the palace tour.

items.name: Murano, glass island
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The lagoon island where Venetian glass has been blown since 1291, watch a live furnace demonstration, tour the Museo del Vetro, and buy directly from the historic furnaces. Arrange a private furnace visit and shipping for a serious chandelier or sculpture; a short vaporetto or water-taxi hop from Fondamente Nove.

items.name: Burano, lace and painted houses
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The most photogenic island in the lagoon, a village of vividly painted fishermen's houses along little canals, and a centuries-old lace tradition shown in the Museo del Merletto. Lunch on lagoon fish here (veg-friendly risottos too), and let the family wander the rainbow lanes.

items.name: Torcello, the oldest island
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: Where Venice began, a near-empty island of grass and reeds with the ancient Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and its extraordinary Byzantine golden mosaics, plus the climbable campanile. Wonderfully peaceful; pair it with Burano next door, or lunch at the storied Locanda Cipriani.

items.name: San Michele, the cemetery island
items.description: The walled island cemetery between Venice and Murano, entered through Codussi's pure white Renaissance church, with cypress avenues and the graves of Stravinsky, Diaghilev and Ezra Pound. A quiet, contemplative half-hour on the way to Murano.

items.name: The Lido di Venezia
items.description: The long sandbar barrier island of beaches and Liberty-era villas, home each September to the Venice Film Festival and the belle-époque grand hotels. Cycle the seafront, take a cabana for a beach day with the children, or dine at the historic Excelsior, a complete change of pace from the stone city.

items.name: Venice Biennale (in season)
items.description: The world's most important art (and, alternate years, architecture) exhibition, spread across the leafy Giardini national pavilions and the vast brick halls of the Arsenale, roughly May to November. The 2026 art edition runs 9 May–22 November; a guided half-day makes the sprawling Arsenale manageable.

items.name: The Arsenale
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The colossal medieval shipyard that built the Republic's fleet, walled, gated by monumental lions, and one of the great sights of industrial history. Much of it opens during the Biennale; the imposing land gate and the lion-guarded entrance repay a look any time.

items.name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia
items.description: A patrician palazzo-museum near Santa Maria Formosa, famous for Carlo Scarpa's exquisite modernist ground floor and garden woven around the canal water. A refined, little-known stop for lovers of art and design, blissfully quiet.

items.name: Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo (San Zanipolo)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon
items.description: The vast Gothic 'pantheon of the doges', burial place of 25 of them, on a handsome campo beside Verrocchio's great equestrian Colleoni statue. Grand and richly furnished; often paired with the nearby Scuola Grande di San Marco façade.

items.name: Ponte dell'Accademia
items.description: The wooden bridge by the Accademia gallery frames the single finest view of the Grand Canal sweeping down to the domes of the Salute, the picture every visitor wants. Best at sunset or in the soft light of early morning.

items.name: Padua day trip
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Padua's fourteenth-century fresco cycles
items.description: Barely 15–25 minutes by fast train, Giotto's world-changing Scrovegni Chapel frescoes (timed booking essential), the huge Basilica of St Anthony, and Europe's oldest botanical garden. An easy, rewarding half- or full-day escape from the lagoon.

items.name: Verona day trip
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, City of Verona
items.description: About an hour by train, the Roman Arena (opera under the stars in summer), Juliet's balcony, and a graceful pink-marble old town on the Adige. Time a visit around the opera festival for an unforgettable evening; a private car makes the door-to-door version effortless.

items.name: Vicenza and the Palladian villas
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, City of Vicenza and the Palladian Villas of the Veneto
items.description: Palladio's own city, 45 minutes by train, the Teatro Olimpico, the Basilica Palladiana, and just outside town the perfect Villa La Rotonda that shaped Western architecture. Combine with a Brenta Riviera cruise past the aristocracy's summer villas on the way back.

items.name: Glam, Enrico Bartolini
items.description: Enrico Bartolini's Venetian two-star, the city's most decorated kitchen, in a frescoed palazzo with a canal garden.

items.name: Oro Restaurant
items.description: Fine Italian cooking inside the Cipriani, the meal begins with a private launch across the water from San Marco.

items.name: Quadri
items.description: The Alajmo family's grand room on St Mark's Square itself, the only starred table with that view.

items.name: Venissa
items.description: Chiara Pavan and Francesco Brutto's 'environmental cuisine' in a walled medieval vineyard, the lagoon on a plate.

items.name: Harry's Bar
credentials: Declared a national landmark by Italy's Ministry of Culture (2001)
items.description: Cipriani's 1931 original, the birthplace of the Bellini and carpaccio, and a declared national landmark.

items.name: Local
items.description: Chef Salvatore Sodano's minimalist, open-kitchen room, one of the most exciting tables in Venice.

items.name: Wistèria
items.area: San Polo (Rio de la Frescada, near the Frari)
items.description: Seasonal contemporary cooking under the wisteria on a quiet lateral canal, intimate and quietly assured.

items.name: Il Ridotto
items.area: Castello (near Campo SS. Filippo e Giacomo, off St Mark's)
items.description: Just nine tables a short stroll from the Basilica, refined Venetian cooking on an intimate scale.

items.name: Al Covo
items.description: A long-loved husband-and-wife room devoted to lagoon fish and unfussy, precise Venetian cooking.

items.name: Ai Gondolieri
items.description: A rare Venetian rarity, a meat-focused kitchen, in the museum quarter near the Guggenheim.

items.name: Antiche Carampane
items.area: San Polo (Rio Terà de le Carampane)
items.description: A hard-to-find, family-run fish osteria beloved by those in the know, no pizza, no menu turistico, no compromise.

items.name: Osteria alle Testiere
items.description: Barely two dozen seats and an ever-changing chalkboard of the day's lagoon catch, a purist's fish room.

items.name: Trattoria Al Gatto Nero
items.description: Burano's most famous kitchen, the risotto de gò (goby-fish risotto) that draws chefs across the lagoon.

items.name: Cip's Club
credentials: Within Belmond Hotel Cipriani (MICHELIN Three Keys)
items.description: The Cipriani's terrace trattoria on the water's edge, pasta and Bellinis with San Marco laid out across the basin.

items.name: Ristorante Riviera
items.description: A refined room on the Zattere waterfront looking to the Giudecca canal, polished Venetian cooking at sunset.

items.name: Vini da Gigio
items.description: A rustic family inn where you can see into the kitchen, proper Venetian fish and meat, and a serious cellar.

items.name: Osteria Anice Stellato
items.description: Imaginative Venetian cooking in the quiet north of Cannaregio, modern takes on regional classics.

items.name: Trattoria Alla Madonna
items.description: A vast, buzzing Rialto institution since 1954, the classic Venetian fish trattoria, done at scale and done well.

items.name: Estro Vino e Cucina
items.description: A modern wine-bar-and-kitchen from two brothers, natural wines and sharp, contemporary Venetian small plates.

items.name: CoVino
credentials: Slow Food, recognised; MICHELIN Guide area listing
items.description: A slow-food micro-restaurant with a short, daily-changing set menu and a thoughtful natural wine list.

items.name: All'Arco
credentials: Widely cited as Venice's finest bacaro; Slow Food / press-recognised
items.description: The benchmark cicchetti counter by the Rialto market, a stand-up plate of the day's best, done impeccably.

items.name: Cantine del Vino già Schiavi (Al Bottegon)
credentials: Cited among Venice's great bacari; Slow Food / press-recognised
items.description: A cult wine bar and cicchetti counter by the gondola boatyard, inventive crostini and a wall of bottles.

items.name: Bar Longhi, The Gritti Palace
credentials: Inside The Gritti Palace (MICHELIN Two Keys, Luxury Collection), a landmark hotel bar
items.description: A jewel-box bar of gilt and Murano glass, opening to a Grand Canal terrace, the most elegant cocktail in Venice.

items.name: Harry's Bar
credentials: Declared a national landmark by Italy's Ministry of Culture (2001)
items.description: The 1931 birthplace of the Bellini, a wood-panelled ground-floor bar that is a piece of Venetian history in itself.

items.name: Caffè Florian
credentials: Founded 1720, the world's oldest continuously-operating café
Historic landmark of Piazza San Marco
items.description: The oldest café in the world still trading, 1720, under the arcades of St Mark's, an orchestra playing on the square.

items.name: Experimental Cocktail Club (Il Palazzo Experimental)
items.area: Giudecca / Dorsoduro (Fondamenta Zattere allo Spirito Santo)
credentials: Part of the acclaimed Experimental Group, internationally recognised bar group
items.description: The Paris-and-London group's Venetian outpost, the city's most serious contemporary cocktails, on the Zattere.

items.name: Bar Terrazza Danieli
credentials: Atop Danieli, Venezia, A Four Seasons Hotel, a landmark rooftop
items.description: The Danieli's rooftop terrace over the lagoon, the Salute, San Giorgio and the basin spread out at sunset.

items.name: Skyline Rooftop Bar, Hilton Molino Stucky
credentials: A landmark rooftop bar, the highest public terrace on the Giudecca waterfront
items.description: An eighth-floor rooftop over the Giudecca canal, the widest panorama of the Venetian skyline over a drink.

plan.heading: 3 days in Venice, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Enter Piazza San Marco before the day-trippers, then tour the Basilica and the Doge's Palace with a private guide via the Secret Itineraries route.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A quiet gondola through the back rii of San Marco, then coffee in the palm court at the Gritti Palace.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Quadri under the arcade, followed by a Bellini at Harry's Bar on the Calle Vallaresso.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Gallerie dell'Accademia at opening, then the Peggy Guggenheim Collection along the canal.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Cross to San Giorgio Maggiore for the Palladian church and the bell-tower view over the lagoon, then an aperitivo at the Cipriani's pool bar on Giudecca.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Oro, the Michelin-starred room at the Belmond Hotel Cipriani, reached by the hotel's private launch.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private motoscafo to Torcello for the mosaics of Santa Maria Assunta, then lunch at Locanda Cipriani.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Murano for a glass furnace visit with a master, then Burano's painted lanes on the way back.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final Venetian dinner at Venissa on Mazzorbo, or Ristorante Local in Castello back in the city.

items.name: San Marco
items.description: The monumental heart, grand hotels and the great sights on the doorstep, but busy and dear; best for a short, central first stay.

items.name: Dorsoduro
items.description: Galleries, the Zattere waterfront and a younger, arty feel; suits those who want to walk everywhere and eat well without the crush.

items.name: Cannaregio
items.description: Residential and genuinely lived-in, with the Jewish Ghetto and good bacari; for repeat visitors who want the real city.

events.name: Carnevale di Venezia
events.note: The masked carnival, costumed balls in private palazzi and the flight of the angel over St Mark's Square.

events.name: Venice Biennale (Art)
events.note: The 61st International Art Exhibition across the Giardini, the Arsenale and pavilions scattered through the city.

events.name: Venice Film Festival
events.note: The world's oldest film festival, on the Lido, red carpets, premieres and the Golden Lion.

events.name: Regata Storica
events.note: A historic pageant of costumed boats and gondola races down the Grand Canal.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in San Marco or the quieter Dorsoduro for canal-side calm away from the day-tripper crush; churches enforce covered shoulders and knees, and the light is best just after the day boats leave at dusk.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Venice Marco Polo (VCE), where a private water-limousine collects you dockside and runs you across the lagoon directly to your hotel's canal entrance.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Move by private water taxi and on foot; there are no cars, so a standing motoscafo or your hotel's boat is how a discerning traveller crosses the city.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Coverage is strong across the city; an Italy or EU eSIM (Airalo, Holafly) works instantly and hotel wifi is reliable.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Euro; cards and contactless are accepted everywhere, keep a little cash for gondoliers and small bacari, and a service charge is usually included so rounding up is enough.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May-June and September-early October are kindest: warm, clear, walkable. Avoid July-August (humid, crowded, mosquito-heavy on the lagoon) and November-December, when acqua alta flooding is most frequent.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No non-stop. Cleanest is Air India non-stop Delhi-Milan Malpensa (~7.5h), then a 40-min hop or ~2.5h car/train to Venice; or one-stop via Gulf hubs (Emirates/Qatar/Etihad) into Venice Marco Polo. For business/first, Qatar Qsuite via Doha is the strongest cabin; arrange a private water-taxi from the airport rather than the public vaporetto.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required for Indian passport holders; routine EU standards. Very safe; the real risk is pickpocketing in crowds around San Marco and Rialto. Tap water is potable throughout.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Easy for vegetarians; Jain is manageable with notice (onion/garlic are common in Venetian cooking, so brief the kitchen). Indian food is limited but present, e.g. Ganesha Ristorante Indiano near the station; better to lean on cicchetti bars and vegetable-forward Venetian menus.
